findings.title: A resourced counterturn
findings.claim: After the first incursion moves through the dwellings, 17:6 gives the turn back against the attackers and furnishes the restored group with wealth, sons, and greater mobilized support; the reversal has the material and social means of a host.
findings.mechanism: The adversarial movement of 17:5 supplies the changed position. In 17:6, raddadna returns the turn to its beneficiaries, amdadnakum names added support, bi-amwal and banin identify material and living resources, and akthara nafiran makes numerical force comparative against them. These words explain how the counterturn is embodied as collective capacity.
findings.reader_payoff: The verse becomes a reversal equipped to sustain a group, rather than a bare change of position.
findings.containment: The granted turn remains the recoverable reading. This relation does not establish moral approval, lasting victory, a narrated battle outcome, or that every son serves as a fighter. The small-group/support facet of nafir is used for capacity only; no headcount is assigned to the enlarged force.

epistemic.reason: The focus alignment resolves all 14 analysis entries, the nominated focus branches have registered carriers and facets, and the prior incursion is explicit in 17:5.

The 17:3 connection's weak reciprocal note calls the link indirect; the focus word sons and exact HFT coordinates keep the reading visible without making it the only account.

findings.containment: The ordinary restored-turn reading remains intact. The conditional sequence supports this local historical pattern without making a universal rule for political outcomes or an inevitable prediction. A live alternative is one historical respite with no general feedback model.

findings.title: Support received, aid sought
findings.claim: Read beside Fātiḥa 1:5, the focus verb for supplying support takes on a recipient-side relation: the resources that enlarge the group are help received within a posture of seeking aid from God, not self-generated strength.
findings.mechanism: The focus MDD carrier names concrete support in wealth and sons; the native 17:20 context already calls extension a gift reaching both opposed groups. The external Fātiḥa verb نستعين, whose supplied root cue names assistance, adds the distinct act of seeking aid from God. The contact shifts the reader's view from provision alone to provision within dependence.
findings.reader_payoff: The restored resources can be seen as support received by a people whose devotional voice asks aid from God.
findings.containment: This is a cross-surah overlay, not a chronological reply or a claim that the people in 17:6 are the speakers of 1:5. Native context already frames provision as a gift; the overlay adds the recipient's posture of seeking help and does not turn political advantage into salvation or moral approval.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and external aid occurrence are explicit in the packet; the recipient-dependence relation is a bounded overlay inference, not a chronological claim.
